# Methodology and limits

*Generated by `scripts/build_methodology.py`; do not edit the table by hand.*

## What the dashboard is
A monitoring tool. It turns public series (FRED, Yahoo Finance, DefiLlama and a few others) into status colours and a composite regime. It does not forecast and it is not financial advice.

## How a status is set
Each indicator has a *warn* and a *crit* threshold and a direction (higher or lower is worse), listed below. Yellow means the warn threshold is crossed, red means crit. Some indicators also use a velocity or percentile rule, described in the indicator's own "Logic" text. The composite score weights the indicator scores using the weights in `config/indicators.json`.

## Where the thresholds come from
They are **heuristics chosen by the maintainer** from commonly cited levels (for example an inverted yield curve, or the Sahm rule trigger at 0.5pp). They were **not fitted by an optimiser**, but they were set **with hindsight of past cycles**, which flatters any backtest. Edit them in `config/indicators.json` and rerun `scripts/build_indicators.py`.

## What the backtest can and cannot say
See *Backtest* for the method. In short: about four recessions and a handful of bear markets exist in the sample, labels overlap, data are revised vintages, and results are optimistic. A high AUC means the signal ranked pre-event months higher in this sample, not that it will do so next time.

## Stress test
Scenario impacts come from simple regressions of monthly returns on rate and oil changes. R-squared is low for most assets, so the unexplained swing dwarfs the modelled effect. Treat outputs as directional scenarios. Assets without enough data use labelled prior assumptions.

## Data quality
Every row shows its observation date and a clock badge when a series is older than its normal cadence. Optional sources (GDELT, Reddit, SEC Form D and mentions, arXiv) can fail without affecting the core dashboard; the Network and Narratives pages label experimental and proxy data.
